summary: A modal for a focused task that interrupts the flow.

pairs.do: sm for confirmations, md for short forms, lg for multi-section work.
pairs.why: The file assigns each width a job. Anything bigger or longer belongs in a Drawer.

pairs.dont: Open a dialog for something the page could say inline.
pairs.do: Keep modals for work that genuinely cannot continue around them.
pairs.why: A modal takes the whole screen hostage. Spend that only where the interruption is the point.

pairs.dont: Label the buttons OK and Cancel.
pairs.do: Say what will happen — Delete endpoint, Save changes.
pairs.why: People read the button, not the paragraph. The verb is where the decision actually gets made.

pairs.dont: Lead with the primary action, or pair it with a ghost button.
pairs.do: Primary last, on the right, paired with a secondary or an outline.
pairs.why: The eye finishes at the right-hand edge, so that is where the commitment belongs — and a ghost beside it reads as a third-tier action rather than the way out.

pairs.dont: Remove the close from a dialog people might open by accident.
pairs.do: Leave the close on; drop it only when an answer is genuinely required.
pairs.why: Escape and the close are the same promise. Taking both away traps anyone who opened it by mistake.

pairs.dont: Open a dialog from inside a dialog.
pairs.do: Advance the content in place, or finish the first task.
pairs.why: Two focus traps and two Escape handlers, and nobody can tell which layer they are answering.

a11y: Radix owns the focus trap, the Escape handler and the aria-modal wiring. A Dialog without a DialogTitle warns in development and leaves the dialog unnamed — give it one even when it is visually hidden.
The close button takes closeLabel as its aria-label; the X glyph is aria-hidden.
Its focus ring is offset against bg/card, not bg/app, because the button sits on the dialog surface.
